summary: Takamatsu Yoshie studied at Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. A founder of Waseda University, he served there as a lecturer from 1908 and as Dean of Letters in 1930.

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. A doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003), Inoue became Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University. He served as associate professor at Shitennoji University in 1991 and at the University of Tokyo (1999–2016).

Takanori Fukita works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University (attested 2017), where he held an appointment, and was appointed special appointment lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani is a religious studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977). He held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1999–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2018).

Takao Hayashi works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University, Kyoto University, and Brown University under David Pingree. His posts include lecturer at Kyoto Women's University (1985–1987) and professor at Doshisha University (1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba. He served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University (~1957–1962). He held professorships at Rissho University (attested 1981), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984), and Mejiro University (attested 1988).

Takao Moriyasu specialized in Iranian/Central Asian studies and history. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, he taught as associate professor at Kanazawa University (1982) and as associate professor and professor at Osaka University (1984; 1994–2012).

Takao Yamagata was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1953–1961). He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1971–1997) and served as president of the Society for Indian Philosophy and Religion (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg under Albrecht Wezler and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as associate professor (~1986–1991) and professor (~1991–2014) at Waseda University.
Takashi Maeda is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995 and 2006).

Takashi Nakao is a Buddhist studies and history scholar. He earned degrees from Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education, taught at Bunkyo University Women's College, and served as emeritus professor at Rissho University (1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo. He became an associate professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
Takashi Yamada is a scholar of sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University. He served as an associate professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (~1999–2007).
Takatoshi Ito is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1981 and 1991).
Takatoshi Nakamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 1978).

Takayasu Higuchi was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942). He was Professor of Archaeology at Kyoto University (~1965–1983) and directed the Institute of Silk Road Studies and Sen-oku Hakuko Kan.

Takayasu Kimura is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University. In 1995, he served as a researcher at the Institute for Contemporary Edification, Shingon-shu Buzan-ha, and lecturer at Taisho University.
Takayasu Suzuki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1988–1998). He became a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2009).
